key_insight: Across binary main-group oxides, oxygen vacancy formation energies track cation reducibility and can be predicted using just crystal reduction potential and band gap.
engineering_relevance: Bulk-property predictions could accelerate oxide screening for solid-oxide fuel cells and solar thermochemical fuel production.
method: Surveyed 39 oxide polymorphs across groups 1, 2, 13, 14, and 15 using r²SCAN density functional theory.
Used ShakeNBreak to locate reconstructed neutral oxygen vacancy ground states.
Fit an interpretable model and retained its two dominant bulk-property descriptors.
evidence_signal: Formation energies span 8 eV, and the two-descriptor model achieves a held-out mean absolute error of 0.31 eV.
watch_item: The study covers neutral vacancies in main-group oxides; prediction errors increase where electron accommodation departs from the cation-reduction picture.
paper_title: Periodic Trends in Oxygen Vacancy Formation Energies Across Binary Main-Group Metal Oxides
